review: First reasoned review of the supplied bytes; names, trait criticalities and classifier calls were treated as leads.

samples.marker: PowerShell stager: policy bypass and encoded remote job; fix placement
samples.identification: PowerShell encoded remote-source background-job stager; no established malware-family attribution
trace: Process execution policy is set to Bypass. A System.Net.WebClient downloads a hardcoded external-IP HTTPS response.
The same response flows through FromBase64String, UTF8.GetString, ScriptBlock.Create, and Start-Job. No local Base64 payload is supplied.
Start-Job runs the script block in a separate child PowerShell process, not in the current interpreter. The job is neither awaited nor received.
samples.balance: Encoded remote execution with policy bypass, a bare IP endpoint and no stated administrative purpose tips likely-malicious over an administrative bootstrap explanation. No theft or final-payload action is claimed. Deployment authorization, remote response, Group Policy effects and runtime completion are unknown.
samples.coverage: Both suspicious objectives and all supported notable capabilities retained; job activation moved to process creation and interpreter execution.

samples.marker: Native DLL dropper: decoded DLL via renamed rundll32; fix claims
samples.identification: Elex-like x86 MFC resource DLL dropper in XZ; external family attribution unconfirmed
trace: Entry 0x42e704 initializes the MFC program; its CWinApp vtable includes InitInstance at 0x401830. Constructor 0x401020 attempts DeleteFileA(argv[1]).

Without argv[1], 0x401220 reads its own image, writes a random temporary executable plus appended bytes, launches a hidden cmd.exe ping-delayed self-copy with the previous path as its argument, then exits.

With argv[1], 0x401450 finds resource GUI/130 and obtains its data. At 0x4014d5, bytes are decoded by i modulo 3: subtract key0+key1, key1, or key0, modulo 256. Initial resource bytes supply keys 0x6e and 0x1f.
It writes the decoded 91144-byte DLL and explicitly restores MZ. A PE parser confirms the DLL and Viewer export at RVA 0xbb50; its interior remains packed.

At 0x4016e3 the system rundll32 path is copied into a source buffer. CopyFileA at 0x40175d stages it under a random executable name. CreateProcessA at 0x401814 starts this renamed loader for the decoded DLL Viewer export. This is a separate path from the ping shell.
samples.balance: Payload scrambling, MZ restoration, random self staging, predecessor deletion and a renamed system loader conceal execution. This concrete chain supports MALICIOUS without inferring the packed DLL final behavior. Runtime success and deployment context are unobserved.
samples.coverage: Two hostile family findings cover ping staging and decoded-resource/renamed-loader behavior. The unsupported ping-to-Viewer link was replaced with a notable API/template co-occurrence observation. Attribute modification is notable.

samples.marker: PHP asset helper: no attacker input; retain read/include capability
samples.identification: Standalone PHP read/include helper; not authenticated as an OpenX distribution
trace: Defines serve_asset($asset), with no top-level invocation or request source.
When called, it echoes file_get_contents($asset), then require_once evaluates the same path. No embedded payload, covert request evaluator or distribution modification is present.

The prior hostile composite also matched different variables, intervening reassignment, and completely quoted PHP source. Its matcher did not bind the file-read path to inclusion or establish hostile intent.
samples.balance: A small unconnected helper using ordinary PHP file APIs is consistent with trusted template preview/execution. A malicious caller or attacker-controlled asset would change a deployment assessment, but neither is supplied. The historical OpenX backdoor had a separate concealed request-eval payload; the collector filename supplies no provenance.
samples.coverage: File output, variable-path evaluation, and the new parser-bound same-path read/include relationship remain notable. Existing PHP request-eval and persistent-backdoor positives retain their detections.

changes.unsupported_claims: The PHP matcher asserted a same-file backdoor without binding paths or attacker input. The PE Viewer matcher joined a ping self-relaunch and a separate renamed-rundll32 launch. Both unsupported intent/linkage claims were corrected while retaining supported operations.
changes.placements: Parsed read/output in fs/read/file/full; variable inclusion in interpreter/eval/source; policy switch text in process/argument/option; Start-Job child execution in process/create/eval and objectives/execution/interpreter/powershell; attribute setters in fs/attributes/flags.
changes.severity: Viewer/ping indicator profile is notable, not hostile. ANSI/Unicode/source SetFileAttributes APIs are now notable with unchanged matchers. No supported attack behavior was demoted.
changes.names: The resource/process profile no longer asserts proximity or requires a temp path it does not test. The Elex any-section identity no longer claims scrambled sections are required.
changes.consumers: Exact IDs, ancestor directory consumers, executable fixture checks and expectations audited. Source and destination membership reviewed. No destination argument/eval/construction selectors double-count the relocated grouping. Generic process/create selectors cease treating policy text as launch evidence and can now observe the actual Start-Job process. Full-file-read selectors gain only a parsed real read/output. The generic fs/file archive co-occurrence no longer treats an attribute-only operation as file content/object I/O.
changes.scope: Other rules in the legacy source leaves remain unchanged. No directory budgets were raised and no sample-name exception was introduced.

validation.pe_mutation: Changing Viewer to Review removes the export-format profile while both hostile family detections survive. The reason for correcting the linkage comes from the original disassembly, not the synthetic control.

losses: Only the unsupported PHP hostile inference and falsely linked hostile Viewer/ping claim were lost. Accurate constituent behavior is retained or relocated. Existing malicious PHP fixture findings and the two hostile Elex findings remain.
classifier_disagreement: PowerShell remains hostile and PHP is unflagged. The malicious PE falls below default ML admission: all root model cls values are 0, probability 0.9294411 at FP level 25000; native member probability is 0.07236425. Two hostile rule findings remain. This is a classifier gap; inaccurate traits were not restored to raise a score.
tooling: atomscan --no-update --mode slow --follow=none; final original scans used CLEAVE_SKIP_CACHE=1. CLEAVE_VALIDATE=0 was needed for atomscan scan runs because its older embedded engine rejects a reviewed directory budget already supported by the current sibling cleave. Final full validation selects that current engine. The model warns spec v18 versus extractor v19. Facts and Rizin disassembly were reviewed directly. No specimen was executed and no specimen endpoint contacted. No fetched dependencies or original PyPI wheels involved.
